nodes.name: ZIF-67 derived hydrothermal substitution
nodes.procedure: The preparation of Yb-Co3O4 HS (5% Yb precursor) experienced the ZIF-67-derived hydrothermal treatment, where the strong coordination of Yb^{3+} with negative sites in ZIF-67 enables partial substitution of Co^{2+} in the CH3OH medium. Upon 60 min of solvothermal treatment in methanol, the ZIF-67 evolves into the hollow sphere structure, consisting of interlaced lamellae for both of YbCo-ZIF and Co-ZIF.

nodes.name: Annealing and Kirkendall diffusion
nodes.procedure: During the annealing process, the low temperature (400°C) allows for the slow oxidation and diffusion metal species, which enables the Kirkendall-type outward diffusion that the inner core is gradually evacuated while the outer shell becomes crystallized. Such diffusion disparity contributes to the uniform hollow-sphere structure with a porous shell and high structural integrity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks of Yb-Co3O4 HS match standard cubic Co3O4 phase (Fd3m, PDF #42-1467) with no Yb-based oxide peaks; peaks shift to lower angles indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline structure of Yb-Co3O4 samples with different Yb contents were determined by X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Figure 1b, the diffraction peaks of Co3O4 are assigned to the standard cubic phase ... implying the lattice expansion of Co3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman active phonon modes of Yb-Co3O4 HS at 688, 480, 615, 520, 196 cm⁻¹ are attenuated and shifted to lower wavenumbers compared to Co3O4 HS, indicating reduced lattice symmetry.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1c displays the comparison of Raman spectra between Yb-Co3O4 HS and Co3O4 HS. For Co3O4, the distinctive peaks at 688 and 480 cm⁻¹ ... indicating the reduction of lattice symmetry.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows enhanced signal intensity at g=2.003 for Yb-Co3O4 HS compared to Co3O4 HS, indicating increased oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron spin resonance (EPR) in Figure 1d shows the enhanced signal intensity at g = 2.003 for Yb-Co3O4-HS, denoting the increased oxygen vacancy.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS analysis of RE-Co3O4 HS (RE=Yb,Gd,Tb,Y) shows consistent +0.27-0.31 eV shift in Co 2p3/2 to higher binding energy vs Co3O4 HS, indicating electron transfer from RE to Co sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis reveals a consistent trend, where the systematic shift toward higher binding energy in the Co 2p3/2 was observed in doped samples (0.31, 0.27, and 0.28 eV, respectively) compared to Co3O4-HS.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals Yb-Co3O4 HS maintains hollow sphere morphology with porous interlaced lamellae after pyrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of YbCo-ZIF with different Yb contents are displayed in Figure S3 ... porous structures appeared on the interlaced lamellae while the overall morphology is still preserved for Yb-Co3O4 HS.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms hollow sphere structure of Yb-Co3O4 HS composed of interlaced lamellae.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanostructures of ZIF-67, YbCo-ZIF, and Yb-Co3O4 HS were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM shows atomic dispersion of Yb in Co3O4 HS with (111) crystal plane exposure (0.296 nm lattice spacing); line scans confirm atomic substitution of Co by Yb.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (AC-HAADF-STEM) image provides direct evidence of the atomic dispersion of Yb sites in Yb-Co3O4-HS ... confirming the successful formation of Yb-Co3O4 phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Yb, Co, O, C in Yb-Co3O4 HS; similar uniform distributions confirmed for Tb-Co3O4 HS, Gd-Co3O4 HS, and Y-Co3O4 HS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping (Figure 2c) reveals a uniform distribution of Yb, Co, O, and C within Yb-Co3O4-HS ... confirming the generality of the synthetic process.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Yb-Co3O4 HS is 92.25 m²/g vs 38.88 m²/g for Co3O4 HS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The hollow sphere architecture ... equips Yb-Co3O4 HS with a larger specific surface area of 92.25 m²g⁻¹ compared with Co3O4-HS of 38.88 m²g⁻¹.
